app.name: HubSpot public OAuth app (HubSpot Developer Platform)

verdict.summary: Creating an OAuth app and connecting your own test account needs no review and takes under an hour. Getting it listed on the HubSpot Marketplace adds a manual listing review plus a minimum of three real unaffiliated installs, and certification adds a six-month and 60-install threshold. Sensitive scopes cannot be used by Marketplace apps.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours to get a working app and test install; roughly 1-3 days of listing prep (legal URLs, setup guide, shared data table, visuals); certification later adds a demo video and security questionnaire.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under 1 hour for your own app in a developer test account (or minutes if you use Composio's managed auth config).
verdict.approval_wait: None to connect your own account. Marketplace listing: initial review aimed at 10 business days; full review and feedback cycle no more than 60 days from feedback. Certification: not applicable until the app has been listed six months and has 60 active unaffiliated installs.

gates.name: Developer app, own account (test install)
gates.unlocks: Create the app, configure OAuth redirect URL and scopes, and connect your own HubSpot account via a test install.
limits: Test install goes to a developer test account via Projects > Distribution > Test installs.
Installer must tick the box authorizing an unverified app before Connect app.
Installing user must be a Super Admin or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes (expires_in 1800); refresh tokens mint new access tokens.
Authorization codes are single-use and must be exchanged quickly.

gates.name: Installs by invited / unaffiliated accounts (unverified app)
gates.unlocks: Other accounts can install and use the app through the OAuth install URL, which is needed to meet the Marketplace minimum of three active installs.
limits: Only accounts that show successful app activity in the last 30 days count as active installs.
Test accounts and accounts affiliated with your organization do not count.
Each unaffiliated account installs with a Super Admin or Marketplace Access user.
Only one app can be in listing review at a time.
gates.time_to_reach: Days to weeks, depending on how fast you can get real accounts to install and use the app

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public, reviewed); certification is a further optional tier
gates.unlocks: App is listed on the HubSpot Marketplace and can be found and installed by any HubSpot account. Certification is a separate later review that adds a certified badge.
limits: Listing review is manual by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team; incomplete fields leave the listing in Draft mode.
Marketplace-listed apps must not request sensitive data scopes.
Marketplace OAuth apps are limited to 110 requests every 10 seconds per installing account, excluding CRM Search.
Certified status is removed if active installs drop below 60 over a trailing six-month period.
Submitting and certification are free, with no revenue share.
gates.time_to_reach: Listing: about 10 business days for initial review, up to 60 days for the full cycle. Certification: at least six months after listing plus 60 active unaffiliated installs, then its own review.

steps.title: Confirm you can create and install an app
steps.detail: Sign in to a HubSpot developer account (the developer account is separate from a HubSpot customer account). Confirm you are a Super Admin in the test account you will install into, or that your user holds HubSpot Marketplace Access. A test account is acceptable for Gate 1.
gotchas: Paid plan requirement for creating an app is not confirmed in the research; check the developer account for any plan prompt.
Installing without Super Admin or Marketplace Access will fail.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Open your portal's applications page and click Create app. Alternatively, on the current developer platform, run the HubSpot CLI (v7.6.0 or later) with hs project create; when prompted, choose the distribution option and select OAuth as the auth type (not a static token).
gotchas: Replace <PORTAL-ID> with your developer account portal ID.
The Create app path is community-sourced; the CLI path is from HubSpot's developer docs.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.detail: Open the app's Auth tab and add the redirect URL. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. It must match the redirect_uri sent in the authorize request exactly. Use https; http is allowed only for localhost testing.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URLs must use a domain, not an IP address.
Composio's default redirect is on backend.composio.dev; if you use your own app, you must add that exact URL here.

steps.title: Declare only the scopes you use
steps.detail: Edit the auth block of app-hsmeta.json, splitting scopes into requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes, then push with hs project upload. Start from the scopes your agent actually calls; do not copy Composio's full default list. Check the Auth tab to confirm the scopes match.
gotchas: Every scope in requiredScopes must appear in the scope parameter of the authorize URL or the authorization page errors.
Scopes that apply only to some users belong in optional or conditional scopes.
Requesting unused scopes conflicts with Marketplace listing rules.

steps.title: Copy client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Run hs project open. Under Project Components, open the app and copy the client ID and client secret from the Auth tab. Store the secret in your secrets manager; do not commit it.
gotchas: If you use Composio's managed auth config, you do not need to enter these in Composio; they are needed only for your own app.

steps.title: Register the app in Composio (own-app path only)
steps.detail: If you are using your own HubSpot app instead of Composio's managed OAuth, create a custom auth config in Composio for the hubspot toolkit and enter the client ID and client secret. Confirm the redirect URI in Composio matches the one set in step 4.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's managed app covers prototyping; a Marketplace listing needs your own app.

steps.title: Run a test install and authorize
steps.detail: Go to Projects > Distribution > Test installs and install the app into your test account. Tick the box to authorize the unverified app, then click Connect app. Use the install URL from the app settings; it includes client_id, redirect_uri and scopes.

values.label: Install URL parameters
values.value: client_id, redirect_uri, scopes (optional_scopes and state allowed)

gotchas: If the authorize page shows a scope error, the scope parameter is missing a required scope.
Authorization codes are single-use; a failed or slow exchange returns AUTHORIZATION_CODE_EXPIRY.

steps.title: Check install logs
steps.detail: Open Development > Monitoring > Logs and select the OAuth tab. Confirm AUTHORIZATION_REQUEST, AUTHORIZATION_GRANT and TOKEN_EXCHANGE events appear for your test install.
gotchas: If the grant is missing, check the redirect URL and scope parameter first.

steps.title: Build token refresh handling
steps.detail: Implement the code exchange and refresh calls to the token endpoint with client_id and client_secret in the body. Refresh before the 30-minute access token expiry and store refresh tokens securely. Verify the token URL before wiring (see open questions).
gotchas: Composio lists https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token; HubSpot docs use v3. Confirm which one you call.
Apps must refresh tokens without asking the user to paste codes or tokens.

steps.title: Get three real unaffiliated active installs
steps.detail: Have at least three accounts outside your organization install the app in production, and make sure each shows successful app activity (OAuth API requests or signed webhook/app-card requests) in the last 30 days. A bare connection does not count. OAuth must be the app's only authorization method.
gotchas: Test accounts and affiliated accounts are excluded.
HubSpot's partner page describes this as three active installs from real customers.

steps.title: Draft listing content
steps.detail: Draft the listing text: app description, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, install button URL, setup guide (specific to setup, install and configuration; no paywall or sign-in), support contact, pricing that matches your website, and the Shared data table matching requested scopes. Use screenshots or video. Do not combine HubSpot's name with the app name or logo.
gotchas: All listing URLs must be live, public and working; allowlist the HubSpot Crawler user agent before submitting.
The setup guide must also cover disconnect and uninstall, with screenshots of each install step including the scope approval screen.

steps.title: Check listing eligibility for scopes
steps.detail: Confirm the app requests no sensitive or highly sensitive scopes (contacts, companies, deals, appointments, custom objects, projects, tickets and their .sensitive / .highly_sensitive variants). If you need them, you must request access from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, which is a separate path and not available for Marketplace listing.
gotchas: Composio's default set includes custom object scopes; confirm whether they fall in the sensitive family before listing.
Sensitive scopes also require an Enterprise subscription on the customer side.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Submit the listing from the developer account. Only one app can be in listing review at a time; additional submissions while one is processing are rejected automatically. Submission and review are free.
gotchas: Incomplete or inaccurate fields leave the listing in Draft mode.
Listing on an unsupported developer platform or API version is blocked.

steps.title: Wait for listing review
steps.detail: Wait for the initial review (aimed at 10 business days). Expect feedback; the full review and feedback cycle should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared.

steps.title: Apply for certification (optional, later)
steps.detail: After the app has been listed for six months with 60 active unaffiliated installs, open Development > App Listings, hover the app, click More, and select Certify app. Submit a YouTube demo video of at least three minutes showing install, configure, use, disconnect and uninstall. Certification also needs a verified domain, OAuth code flow using all requested scopes, a security questionnaire, and a passing security assessment.

values.label: Menu path
values.value: Development > App Listings > More > Certify app

gotchas: Promotional sales videos are rejected.
Your app must call the Uninstall App API endpoint on removal, and the video must show the endpoint call and removal from Connected Apps.
Certification must be renewed every two years.

steps.title: Keep reliability above threshold
steps.detail: Keep the average API success rate above 95%, keep errors under 5% of daily requests, and respect the per-account limit of 100 inbound requests every 10 seconds. Add backoff on 429 responses so bursts do not trip the limit.
gotchas: A 429 is returned for all calls once a limit is exceeded.
Burst 429s caused one reported certification failure.

requirements.detail: A HubSpot developer account, an app tied to it, and a HubSpot account to install into (a test account is fine).

requirements.item: Super Admin or Marketplace Access to install
requirements.detail: The installing user must be a Super Admin or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
Redirect URLs must use https (http only for localhost), use a domain not an IP, and match redirect_uri exactly.

requirements.item: Required scopes in the authorize URL
requirements.detail: The scope parameter must include every required scope or the authorization page errors.
Test installers must tick the box authorizing an unverified app before Connect app.
At least three active unique installs in unaffiliated production accounts with activity in the past 30 days, OAuth as sole auth method, and agreement to the Technology Partner Program Agreement.
Live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, Install button URL, setup documentation URL, support contact, pricing matching website, and Shared data table matching scopes.
Setup guide must be public (no paywall or sign-in), app-specific, with install and configuration steps.
Marketplace-listed apps must not request sensitive data scopes; unused scopes must be removed.
Apps on unsupported platform or API versions cannot be listed or certified.
Classic CRM cards are not supported for listed apps; use UI extension app cards.

Six months listed, 60 active unaffiliated installs, verified domain, OAuth code flow with all scopes, security assessment and questionnaire, demo video of at least three minutes, Uninstall App API call.

scopes.effect: Sensitive scopes cannot be used by Marketplace-listed apps. Access needs a request to HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, and Super Admins must reauthorize on an Enterprise account. Existing users must re-authorize after publication.

scopes.scope: Sensitive families: contacts, companies, deals, appointments, custom objects, projects, tickets
scopes.effect: Same as above; these families are excluded from listed apps unless HubSpot allowlists them.
Research did not confirm whether these fall in the sensitive family. Confirm before listing.

scopes.scope: Composio default scope set (about 40 scopes, including marketing_events, quotes, custom schemas)
scopes.effect: Trim to scopes the app uses. Unused scopes must be removed for listing.
Optional scopes are dropped automatically for accounts without access to that tool, so use them for features that only some accounts have.

blockers.symptom: Listing or certification rejected because the app runs on an unsupported developer platform or API version (HubSpot community post says apps on unsupported platform versions will be rejected from November 2, 2026).
blockers.cause: The app was built on a platform or API version HubSpot no longer supports for listings. The full effective requirement was not retrieved.
blockers.fix: Confirm the app is on the current developer platform (versions 2025.2 or 2026.03 per the CLI docs) and CLI v7.6.0 or later. Upgrade before submitting, given the stated November 2, 2026 date.

blockers.symptom: Listing requires removing scopes; app cannot be listed while it requests sensitive data scopes.
blockers.cause: Marketplace-listed apps cannot use sensitive data scopes. Self-serve access is not available.
blockers.fix: Remove sensitive scopes for the listing version. If the product truly needs them, request access from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team and plan for re-authorization.
blockers.contact: HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team (channel not confirmed in research)

blockers.symptom: Listing stays in Draft mode, or submission is rejected for incomplete fields.
blockers.cause: Missing or non-live listing URLs, mismatched pricing, or a Shared data table that does not match requested scopes.
blockers.fix: Make every listing URL live and public, allowlist the HubSpot Crawler user agent, and make the Shared data table match the scopes.

blockers.symptom: Listing review or certification fails on reliability: API success rate below 95%, or 429 errors.
blockers.cause: Burst traffic exceeds the per-account limit of 100 inbound requests every 10 seconds, or errors exceed 5% of daily requests.
blockers.fix: Add rate limiting and backoff for 429 responses, and check error rate in logs before submitting. Marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 110 requests every 10 seconds per installing account.

blockers.symptom: A second listing submission is automatically rejected.
blockers.cause: Only one app can be in listing review at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the current review to finish before submitting another app.

blockers.symptom: Install fails with AUTHORIZATION_CODE_EXPIRY in the OAuth logs.
blockers.cause: The single-use authorization code was not exchanged within the short window.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately after the redirect and avoid blocking work before the token call.

blockers.symptom: Certification not available; the app cannot apply.
blockers.cause: Certification needs six months listed, 60 active unaffiliated installs, and enough API traffic.
blockers.fix: Plan certification as a later phase; do not treat it as part of the first listing.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth config to prototype without registering a HubSpot app. Register your own HubSpot public app (client ID and secret) when you need your own branding, control over redirect URIs and scopes, or a Marketplace listing. Composio's default scope set is broad (about 40 scopes); trim to what your app uses before listing. Composio's default redirect URI is on backend.composio.dev. Verify the token URL (v1 vs v3) before wiring.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit record shows managed OAuth is available for HubSpot, with HubSpot's authorize URL and token URL and a default redirect URI on Composio's backend.
A developer needs a HubSpot developer account, an app tied to it, and a HubSpot account to install into (a test account is acceptable).
Installing an app into a HubSpot account requires the installing user to be a Super Admin or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
Apps on the current developer platform are created with the HubSpot CLI via hs project create; CLI must be v7.6.0 or later; the CLI prompts for distribution and auth type.
In the developer account UI, the app is created from the applications page via Create app, then configured on the Auth tab for redirect URLs and scopes.
For a developer-platform app, client ID and secret are found by running hs project open, opening the app under Project Components, and copying from the Auth tab.
Required, conditionally required and optional scopes are declared in the auth block of app-hsmeta.json and pushed with hs project upload.
Redirect URLs must use https in production (http only for localhost), must use a domain not an IP, and must match redirect_uri in the authorize request.
The scope parameter in the authorize URL must include every required scope or the authorization page shows an error; optional scopes are dropped for accounts lacking access.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes (expires_in 1800); refresh tokens mint new access tokens; code exchange and refresh go to /oauth/v3/token with client_id and client_secret in the body.
The authorization code is single-use and must be exchanged within a short window; an expired code is logged as AUTHORIZATION_CODE_EXPIRY.
Installation attempts are reviewed under Development > Monitoring > Logs, OAuth tab, with AUTHORIZATION_REQUEST, AUTHORIZATION_GRANT and TOKEN_EXCHANGE events.
Unverified apps can be installed for testing in a developer test account via Projects > Distribution > Test installs; the installer must tick a box before Connect app.
Marketplace apps cannot self-serve Sensitive Data scopes; the developer requests access from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, and existing users must re-authorize.
Sensitive scopes cover contacts, companies, deals, appointments, custom objects, projects and tickets; highly sensitive scopes are a further separate set.
After sensitive scopes are granted, a Super Admin must reopen the authorization URL, select an Enterprise account, and click Connect App; Sensitive Data is limited to Enterprise accounts.
Marketplace-listed apps must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes, and app cards must not display sensitive information.
Every scope an app requests at install must actually be used; unused scopes must be removed; conditional scopes should be declared as conditionally required or optional.

Listing minimums: OAuth as sole authorization method, unique app, at least three active unique installs in unaffiliated production accounts with activity in the past 30 days, and agreement to the Technology Partner Program Agreement.
Active installs count only accounts with successful app activity in the last 30 days; test and affiliated accounts are excluded; a bare connection does not count.

Listing requires live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, an Install button URL, setup documentation URL, a support contact, pricing matching the website, and a Shared data table matching scopes.
Incomplete or inaccurate listing fields leave the listing in Draft mode; listing URLs must be live and public; HubSpot recommends allowlisting the HubSpot Crawler user agent.
The listing's setup guide must not sit behind a paywall or sign-in, must be specific to app setup, and must include install and configuration steps.
The setup guide must also cover disconnecting and uninstalling, include screenshots of each install step including the scope approval screen, and describe effects on user data.
Listing review is manual by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team, aiming for an initial review within 10 business days; full review and feedback cycle no more than 60 days from feedback.
Only one app can be in listing review at a time; additional submissions while one is processing are automatically rejected.
Submitting a listing and going through certification review are both free, with no revenue share.
Certification requires the app to be listed at least six months and have at least 60 active unique unaffiliated installs (test accounts excluded), plus needed API traffic.
To apply for certification, open Development > App Listings, hover the app, click More, select Certify app, and submit a YouTube URL for the demo video; one app at a time.
The demo video must be at least three minutes, show install, configure, use, disconnect and uninstall; promotional sales videos are rejected.

Certification requires a verified domain, OAuth authorization code flow using all requested scopes, a security best-practices assessment, and a security questionnaire covering encryption, access controls and token lifecycle.
Apps must not ask users to paste OAuth codes or tokens; the app must request, manage and refresh tokens without user involvement.
Certification requires calling the Uninstall App API endpoint when a customer removes the app; the demo must show the disconnect, the call, and removal from Connected Apps.
Certification reliability criteria include an average API success rate above 95% and respecting 100 inbound requests every 10 seconds per account; one feedback example cites 429 burst errors.
Error requests should not exceed 5% of total daily requests; a 429 is returned for all calls once a limit is exceeded.
Apps must use a supported developer platform and API version to be listed or certified; apps on unsupported versions cannot be listed.
Classic CRM cards are no longer supported since June 16, 2025 and cannot be used by listed apps; UI extension app cards are the replacement.
Certification is valid on a rolling basis for two years and must be renewed; HubSpot sends a renewal notice three months before.
Certified status is removed if active installs drop below 60 over a trailing six-month period; a rejected applicant can re-apply after six months.
Marketplace OAuth apps are limited to 110 requests every 10 seconds per installing account, excluding the CRM Search API.
Community posts say public OAuth apps have no daily call cap; this is unverified against HubSpot's own docs.
HubSpot's partner page says listing requires at least three active installs from real customers using the integration before submission.
The install URL in app settings includes client_id, redirect_uri and scopes as query parameters, and can carry optional_scopes and state.
Probe: app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize is live and returned a 200 HubSpot OAuth page for an invalid client_id; this confirms the endpoint exists, not the rejection text.
The developer portal URL pattern is app.hubspot.com/developer/<PORTAL-ID>/applications, where Create app is shown for a developer account.
Listings should include screenshots or video; HubSpot's brand rules forbid combining HubSpot's name with the app name or logo.
The app must not fit or deliver functionality that would exclusively serve customers within HubSpot's restricted industries.
Certification requests get a response from the Ecosystem Quality team within 10 business days; full review no more than 60 days from feedback.
Composio's managed OAuth config for HubSpot carries a default scope set of about 40 scopes, including marketing_events, quotes, custom object and schema scopes.

open_questions: Whether a paid HubSpot plan is needed to create a developer app was not confirmed; only the free developer account and the Super Admin / Marketplace Access install requirement are documented.

A May 2026 HubSpot community post says apps on unsupported platform versions will be rejected starting November 2, 2026, but the retrieved text was cut off. Today is 2026-10-28, so this may be about five days away. Confirm the effective rule and your app's platform version now.
Token URL: Composio lists https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v1/token; HubSpot's docs use /oauth/v3/token. Confirm which one Composio calls before wiring your own app.
Whether Composio's managed app can be used for a Marketplace listing was not confirmed; the guide assumes a Marketplace listing requires your own registered app.

Whether an unlisted public app can be installed by outside accounts without going through listing was only partly confirmed. OAuth is required for multi-account installs and the install flow shows an unverified-app checkbox.
Public-app daily call cap is unresolved: official docs give 110 per 10 seconds per installing account; community posts say no daily cap, which is unverified.
Whether Composio's custom object and schema scopes (crm.objects.custom.read, crm.schemas.custom.read) fall in the sensitive family was not confirmed.
No official list of scopes triggering review beyond the sensitive and highly sensitive families was found.
Real-world approval times were not found; only HubSpot's documented 10 business day initial review and 60-day cycle are available.
The developer portal sits behind login and was not probed; UI labels are from docs and community sources.
